R1.description: A table first cell, a bold label, a heading label and a numbered item accept the D2 label forms (`F1`, `3a`, `6.1`, `6b-split` among them) with every existing label (a letter, one or two digits) unchanged and flow ids still `flow-N` in order

R2.description: A shape that recognises some items and not others refuses with `checklist_unrecognised`, naming the unrecognised items and `recognised` of `total`, in each of the four shapes, instead of returning the partial list; words, sub-labels, case tables and prose inside a flow are not refused; a newly accepted table label nested in a flow of another shape stays in that flow, so a checklist the old parser read as headings, bold labels or numbered items keeps every flow (D7)

R3.description: The refusal keeps its code, shape list and remedy, adds the D3 evidence, and names a table's first cells when nothing is found; the two Manager checklists are read as five flows each

R4.description: The measured history shows no checklist read completely by the old parser that the new one refuses for a name that is not a flow; the only checklist it reads differently without a refusal is a named, reasoned difference (`settings-and-telemetry`, 16 flows to 29, D6), pinned by a test, and no flow text the old parser read is lost

R5.description: The shape wording, the guides and the roadmap state the rule; no setting, option, exit code, gate or result contract changes
